title: Companies Led by Indian-Origin Chiefs Now Worth $15 Trillion, Up 53%, Hurun Finds
excerpt: The second HSBC Hurun Global Indians List counts 236 Indian-origin CEOs, chairpersons, and founders across 200 companies headquartered outside India, with more than 70% of the value in AI-driven firms.
body:
• The HSBC Hurun Global Indians List 2026 values the 200 most valuable companies led by Indian-origin leaders at a combined US$15 trillion, up 53% from US$9.9 trillion in the inaugural 2024 edition.
  • The second edition of the list recognises 236 CEOs, MDs, chairpersons, and founders across 200 companies, all headquartered outside India, with valuations measured at a June 25, 2026 cut-off.
  • More than 70% of the list's value sits in companies driven by AI, and the entry cut-off more than doubled, from US$1.2 billion to US$2.5 billion; 76 companies appear for the first time.
  • Most of the leaders did not found their companies: 125 of the 236 were selected by global boards to lead, a shift the list's authors call its most striking finding.

HSBC India and Hurun India on Thursday released the HSBC Hurun Global Indians List 2026, ranking the 200 most valuable companies in the world led by leaders of Indian origin. The combined value of the companies on the list stands at US$15 trillion, up 53% from US$9.9 trillion in the inaugural 2024 edition, according to the list's release, reported by NewsInPics and Rediff MoneyWiz.

Companies were ranked by value — market capitalisation for listed companies and Hurun Research valuations for unlisted ones — with a cut-off date of June 25, 2026. Of the 200 companies featured, 127 are listed and 73 are privately held, and all are headquartered outside India. This is the second edition of the list, which highlights the role of the Indian diaspora in the global economy.

An AI-Heavy List

The list's value is concentrated in technology. More than 70% of the value on the list sits in companies driven by AI, and the release points to Sundar Pichai at Alphabet — which the list's coverage notes has overtaken Microsoft in market valuation — and Satya Nadella at Microsoft, alongside a newer generation that includes Aravind Srinivas at Perplexity and Aman Sanger at Cursor.

"More than 70% of the value on this list sits in companies driven by AI. From Sundar Pichai at Alphabet and Satya Nadella at Microsoft to Aravind Srinivas at Perplexity and Aman Sanger at Cursor, Indian-origin leaders are shaping the technology that will define the next 20 years."

— HSBC Hurun Global Indians List 2026 commentary

The bar for entry rose sharply with the valuations. The cut-off to make the list more than doubled, from US$1.2 billion in 2024 to US$2.5 billion in 2026, and 76 companies enter the list for the first time this year.

Chosen, Not Just Founders

The finding the list's authors single out is about how these leaders got their jobs. Of the 236 Global Indians recognised, 125 did not found their companies — they were selected by global boards to lead them. That professional-manager majority, spanning chief executives, managing directors, chairpersons, and founders, is what the release calls the most striking finding of this year's edition, ahead of the US$15 trillion headline itself.

The list measures company value, not personal wealth: the US$15 trillion is the combined market capitalisation and estimated valuation of the 200 companies these leaders run. What it tracks, year to year, is how much of the world's corporate value sits in companies whose top job is held by a person of Indian origin — and on the 2026 numbers, that share grew by more than half in two years.
